8-Day Pushkar Music Retreat


8-Day Winter Music Retreat — Pushkar, Ajmer, Rajasthan, India

Come to Pushkar to find your voice, deepen your devotion, and learn music in a peaceful spiritual atmosphere.

For 8 days at Krishna Music School, you will learn singing, mantra chanting, kirtan, bhajan and harmonium with personal guidance, correct technique and devotional feeling.

Krishna Music School — teaching authentic Indian music to seekers from over 50 countries since 2007

Join us for a beautiful and inspiring Singing, Mantra Chanting, Kirtan, Bhajan and Harmonium Music Retreat at Krishna Music School in the spiritual town of Pushkar, Rajasthan.

This 8-day retreat is specially designed for music lovers, beginners and spiritual seekers who want to learn Indian devotional music in a peaceful, traditional and heart-opening environment.

Pushkar is known for its holy lake, ancient temples, evening aarti, desert light and devotional atmosphere. Here, music does not feel like a performance. It feels like practice, prayer and self-discovery.

What Makes This Pushkar Retreat Special

At Krishna Music School, our main focus is not only enjoying music. Our deeper focus is helping students learn how to sing correctly, understand melody and rhythm, and play harmonium with proper feeling.

Many people come to music with love, but without technique. They sing with tension. They lose pitch. They feel shy about their voice. They want to chant or lead kirtan, but they do not know where to begin.

This retreat gives you a clear foundation. You will receive personal guidance in voice practice, harmonium techniques, rhythm, devotional singing and the emotional expression behind Indian music.

During the retreat, you will train in:

  • Singing and vocal techniques for better pitch, breath and tone
  • Mantra chanting with correct pronunciation, rhythm and feeling
  • Kirtan and Bhajan singing in traditional devotional style
  • Harmonium playing for melody, scale practice and self-accompaniment
  • Understanding melody and rhythm so your singing becomes more stable and expressive

Why Pushkar Is the Perfect Place for Music

Pushkar is one of Rajasthan’s most spiritual towns. The sound of temple bells, evening aarti at Pushkar Lake, devotional singing, peaceful lanes and desert air create a special atmosphere for learning music.

In Pushkar, music naturally connects with devotion. A mantra is not just a melody. A bhajan is not just a song. A kirtan is not just a group activity. Each one becomes a way to listen, feel and express something deeper.

During the retreat, you will also experience the sacred and cultural side of Pushkar through selected visits and evening experiences, including Pushkar Lake, Brahma Temple, Savitri Mata Temple and Rangji Temple.

Special Pushkar experiences during the retreat may include:

  • Evening Aarti and Pooja at the holy Pushkar Lake
  • Visit to the famous Brahma Temple
  • Mountain visit to Savitri Mata Temple
  • Visit to Rangji Temple near Krishna Music School
  • Time to explore local markets, temples and the spiritual atmosphere of Pushkar

November Batch Special — Pushkar Camel Fair Atmosphere

The November 2026 batch is special because it falls close to the world-famous Pushkar Camel Fair season. During this time, Pushkar becomes full of color, folk music, cultural programs, local markets, traditional Rajasthani life and village energy.

Because official fair activities and dates can vary, we describe this honestly: the November batch gives you the chance to experience the special atmosphere and opening energy around Pushkar Camel Fair season, depending on the final local schedule.

During the fair season, Pushkar may offer:

  • Traditional Rajasthani cultural activities
  • Folk music and dance performances
  • Cultural programs and fairground celebrations
  • Camel fair atmosphere and local markets
  • Authentic Rajasthani traditions and village culture

What We Teach — and Why It Works

Your Voice Is Not Broken. It Is Untrained.

Many students arrive saying, “I cannot sing.” But often the problem is not the voice. The problem is that nobody has shown them how to use the voice correctly.

In this retreat, we help you understand how to sing with better breath, better pitch, better mouth placement and better awareness. You will not only copy songs. You will learn the foundation behind singing.

Real teaching, real connection — personal guidance in voice, harmonium and devotional music

In 8 days you will learn to consciously use:

  • Your breath for natural and stable singing
  • Your belly, chest and throat for better voice support
  • Your mouth, jaw and tongue for clearer notes
  • Your hands and voice together while playing harmonium
  • Your feeling and expression while singing mantras, kirtan and bhajan
Register for the Pushkar Music Retreat

Your 8 Days — What Actually Happens

Days 1–2: Finding Your Musical Foundation

We begin with the basics of Indian music: Sa, Sargam, breath, pitch and listening. You will learn how to find your root note and how to begin singing without forcing your voice.

These first two days help you build confidence. You start to hear your voice differently. You also begin harmonium practice step by step.

Day 3: Voice, Breath and Body Awareness

Your voice does not work alone. Breath, posture, mouth position and emotional state all affect your singing. On this day, you will learn how to coordinate your body and voice for a more natural sound.

Days 4–5: Harmonium, Melody and Rhythm

You will practice harmonium with your voice. You will learn how to follow melody, stay in rhythm and sing simple devotional phrases while playing.

This is where many students feel the joy of music becoming practical. The harmonium starts to support your singing, and your singing starts to guide your hands.

Day 6: Mantra Chanting and Devotional Expression

Mantra chanting is not only about repeating words. It is about pronunciation, rhythm, melody and feeling. You will learn how to chant with calmness, clarity and devotion.

Days 7–8: Kirtan, Bhajan and Integration

The final days bring everything together. You will practice kirtan and bhajan singing, group chanting, harmonium accompaniment and devotional expression.

You leave with a clearer voice, a stronger foundation, simple harmonium skills and a practice you can continue after the retreat.

What You Leave With

  • Better voice control — sing with more awareness, confidence and stability
  • Breath and pitch practice — understand how to stay steady while singing
  • Harmonium foundation — play simple melodies and support your own singing
  • Mantra chanting skills — chant with pronunciation, rhythm and feeling
  • Kirtan and Bhajan practice — understand devotional singing in a group setting
  • Understanding of melody and rhythm — build a real foundation, not just memorized songs
  • A spiritual music experience in Pushkar — temple visits, lake aarti and cultural connection
  • A daily music practice — something you can continue at home

Common Questions

I am a complete beginner. Can I join this retreat?

Yes. This retreat is beginner-friendly. You do not need previous musical experience. The teaching starts with foundation, listening, voice practice, simple melody and harmonium basics.

Which batch should I choose?

All four batches follow the same core retreat structure. November has the special atmosphere around Pushkar Camel Fair season. December, January and February offer peaceful winter weather and a calm learning atmosphere in Pushkar.

Is the November batch during Pushkar Camel Fair?

The November batch is close to Pushkar Camel Fair season and may allow students to experience the opening atmosphere, local culture and fair-related energy depending on the final local schedule. We avoid overpromising exact fair activities because official schedules can vary.

Are accommodation and meals included?

No. Accommodation and meals are not included in the retreat fee. Pushkar has many guesthouses, hotels, cafés and local restaurants, so students can choose according to their comfort and budget.

How many students are in each batch?

Each batch is limited to a maximum of 10 students. This keeps the retreat personal, focused and supportive.

Do I need to bring my own harmonium?

No. Harmonium use during class is included. If you already have your own harmonium and want to bring it for extra practice, you may contact us before arrival.

Can I join for fewer than 8 days?

The retreat is designed as an 8-day progressive journey. Each day builds on the previous day. For the best result, we recommend attending the full retreat.

What language are classes in?

Classes are taught in English. Krishna Music School has experience teaching international students from many countries and explains Indian music in a clear and simple way.

How do I register?

You can register through the Google Form on this page. You can also contact Krishna Music School by WhatsApp at +91 99286 58520 or email krishnamusicschoolpushkar@gmail.com.

About Krishna Music School

Founded in 2007 near Rangji Temple in Pushkar, Rajasthan, Krishna Music School has taught authentic Indian classical and devotional music to students from over 50 countries. The school teaches singing, harmonium, mantra chanting, kirtan, bhajan, tabla, dholak, violin, guitar and raga in a traditional and personal learning atmosphere.

The teaching approach is patient, practical and rooted in the traditional guru-shishya spirit. Whether you are a complete beginner or already practicing music, the goal is to help you understand your voice, your instrument and the feeling behind Indian devotional music.
